title: Milt Hinton: the "Judge" nickname and long friendship
summary: Jones knew Milt Hinton from the 1940s through John Levy; they call each other Judge, and Milt was his contractor.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You were mentioning Milt Hinton off the tape. How far back do you and Milt Hinton go?

Okay. Now, I think I mentioned one thing to you off the tape, was -- in Stanley Dance's book, "The World of Duke Ellington," where Milt Hinton and Ray Nance went to the same high school together, and Ray Nance was a phenomenal talent, as we both know.

But he mentioned in that book, he says he couldn't move to the first chair because the guy that really held the first chair down was the -- became a very famous bass player, Milton Hinton. And that was a -- I don't know if Milt even knows this was stated by Nance, because I haven't talked to Milt lately.
Now, as far as going back with him, oh, boy. I've been knowing Milt since about the '40s. Because John Levy and Milt went to school together, you know.
And that's how I knew him.
So you knew him in Chicago.
Yeah. Well, no, I met him in New York. I knew of him in Chicago. Because he was one of the prominent musicians that left Chicago and became successful.
You were telling me that you and Milt called each other Judge.

Oh, I don't know. Let's see, how did -- it's almost like a standard nickname for each other. You know, Milt has a very high voice. "Hey, Judge?" That's the way he sounds, you know. And I said, "Hey, Judge." And he sent me a birthday card, as I was telling you. He says, "I hereby sentence you to 30 days of good music." And I've got to call him back, because I didn't know that he knew when my birthday was. That was a real pleasant surprise, you know? But you'd be surprised -- well, to watch him work, as of today, I told John Levy, I said, "Man, you should see Milt A." And he looks like a teenager.
And he's playing like one. He's got that great positive attitude, and you can't beat that, really.

Yeah. He's got it. It's built in him, you know? And he's so well rounded as a musician, I don't think you're going to find many any better than Milt, or as good. Because he's -- in fact, when I was beginning to write, back east, Milt was my contractor. I used to split it with Milt, when Milt was too busy I would get Clarke Terry.
